source_refs.note: Topic 8.4.1 (PDF 200-201, printed 197-198). Long question 4 is answered.

blocks.text: Ethical research makes findings trustworthy and respects the rights of those involved. Following ethical guidelines avoids harm, misinformation and unfairness, and makes results credible and useful to others. Falsifying data or copying others' work without credit (plagiarism) is unethical: it leads to wrong conclusions and damages the researcher's reputation.

blocks.prompt: Discuss the importance of research ethics for credible findings and how unethical practices affect the research community and society (long question 4).
blocks.explanation: Ethics make findings trustworthy: honest data, credited sources and fair, unbiased analysis let others rely on and build on the results, and consent and confidentiality protect participants. Unethical practices such as fabricated data, plagiarism or ignoring consent produce false conclusions, waste other researchers' time and money, damage trust in science and can harm society when decisions on health, policy or safety rest on them; they also ruin the researcher's reputation.

items: Ethics make research trustworthy; fraud and plagiarism mislead others and destroy trust.
